notes.title: New years changes
notes.notes:
Happy New Year! 

While I was off visiting family in law, I realized I had some more problems with the game so I fixed them this morning.
1. the hands would disappear because of some code that let you select different hands, I turned it off.
2. someone mentioned the game did not work with the VIVE headset because the camera is in the head. I made the head invisible.
3. I despised the recoil on some of the long guns so i lessened it.

That is it, thank you!

notes.title: Long time no see! I made a big update!
notes.notes:
Greetings.
It has been a long while since I updated the game last, but I had some free time and wanted to make it better. Hopefully the few of you who still might play it let me know what you think of the changes.
1.	Full body avatar. I thank “Johnny5” from the VRIF discord for his wonderful tutorials on how to add full body IK to VR. I was lazy however and I still used the default hands rig and just attached them to the body. I did this because it would be more work to retarget hands to fit as nicely as the originals did, and I just did not want to do that.
This in turn means hands will glitch a bit and sometimes bug out, but not usually so. 

2.	The second section of the levels, the “maze sections” have been slightly visually improved, at least I think they are. Also, they no longer end with a stupid purple teleport at the end, now they have a door with a stupid purple teleport that makes more sense!

3.	The player still has the slow down ability attached to the Y button, but now when you shoot the guns, you fire off actual projectiles more powerful than regular gunfire. These will kill most enemies in a few hits, look cool and they will knock them off their feet and flying around.

4.	I brought back the dynamic ragdoll enemies. So now you can punch them around and knock them over with your guns and a new baseball bat. Be warned: the baseball bat is hard to use and can cause bugginess, but it is kind of fun! Oh, only the small skeletons, zombies and mummies are dynamic ragdolls, the bigger more bullet spongy enemies cannot be knocked around.

5.	The number of enemies in the maze section of the levels was reduced. The few of you that have played and spoken said they were to many.

6.	Some textures in the Mayan/Aztec levels were changed. I was never satisfied with them.

7.	A knife was added, and the baseball bat have blood effects that spawn on contact with enemies. Enjoy!

I think that is it. I hope you enjoy the game as much as I enjoy continuing to work on it!
I will update the videos and pictures on the store page also.

notes.title: Belongs in a Museum Version 8
notes.notes:
Good evening! 
If it is evening for you. ( It is evening here in Asia) 
This is the newest version of It Belongs in a Museum. 

Here is what has changed.
1. The active ragdolls were taken off the melee enemies so they no longer can be punched and knocked down :( I figured it was better to have more frames than the occasional laugh at punching a skeleton or zombie into the dirt.
2. A new BLUE backpack! Now at the beginning of levels, is a new blue backpack. you must now pick up the treasures in the levels instead touching them to the old brown backpack and automatically collecting them into cash. When you pick up treasures, you can take them back to the menu and put them into the old brown back pack on the table to collect the cash. You can also hold onto your treasures and guns (if you have the space in the backpack) into the next level. The blue backpack will save all the items put in it, so this would make it easy to dupe stuff... a problem I have yet to fix.
3. your health does not reset/refill after you leave an area through a door portal or ground portal. now if you die and return to the museum your health "should" refill *crosses fingers* and in between levels if your health is low, you must purchase the health vial and use it to heal. 

That is it! I know this might make it harder for some, but this is how I had intended it from the beginning when I had imagined it almost 3 years ago. Now that I have learned new coding tricks and new ways to do things, I have applied them to get one step closer to perfecting the game (in my mind at least)

-Coffeeserpent

notes.title: Small changes
notes.notes:
Good Morning.

This is just a small change in the first eternal temple level. I made it a night time scene as I liked it better that way and I covered up the hole in the floor behind the starting area that leads to the skull key. It was annoying me that I could not jump the gap.

notes.title: New changes to "It belongs in a Museum"
notes.notes:
Good Morning,

So its been a while and if you are still paying attention to my little game, here is what has changed:

- Turned off the highlight effect when shooting monsters: it was actually starting bother me but if you want it back I will find a way to make it an option

- Added a tutorial from the main menu library scene. It is between the start and quit button. It should explain in a hopefully decent AI voice how to play the game.

- Added some backgrounds to out door stages as it made them look more alive and fun to be in. 

- changed the textures in the Aztec level as I believed it looked funny with it being colorful and not ancient-like enough. 

Thanks for reading, I will make more changes as requested and as I have time.

CoffeeSerpent

I will endeavor to push out fixes to things as best as I can but in the next two months I have "professor stuff" that requires much of my time, so send me your needs and I will do my best to fix it.

CoffeeSerpent
